sanskrit_verse:
पितापितामहो यस्य जीवेच च प्रपितामहः /
त्रिंशत् समा तु या भुक्ता भूमिर् अव्याहता परैः // BrhS_1,७.३६
transliteration: pitāpitāmaho yasya jīvec ca prapitāmahaḥ / triṃśat samā tu yā bhuktā bhūmir avyāhatā paraiḥ
sph_interpretive_translation: Where the paternal grandfather, the great-grandfather, and the great-great-grandfather of a person are alive, and the land has been enjoyed undisturbed by others for thirty years, that land belongs inherently to that lineage.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows through uninterrupted patrilineal continuity
Causation is established through generational presence and territorial harmony
Capacity-based responsibility arises from ancestral custodianship
Restoration logic validates ownership through time-bound uncontested enjoyment
Consciousness alignment occurs when lineage integrity is recognized in material inheritance
executable_legal_axioms: IF (paternal ancestor chain >= 3 generations alive) AND (land enjoyed without dispute for 30 years) THEN (title is intrinsically validated)
IF (lineage continuity is unbroken) AND (no external contest recorded in 30 solar cycles) THEN (territorial right auto-restored)
IF (ancestral dwelling axis active) AND (no vyāhata claim within triṃśat samā) THEN (bhūmir svāmī remains unchanged)
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes an irrefutable threshold where ancestral continuity and temporal peaceability create inherent title. The court must recognize such claims prima facie, with burden shifting to disturbers of possession, aligning judicial process with dharma-rooted proprietorship.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: This rule reflects pramāṇa-based causality: uninterrupted generational life and peaceful tenure manifest rightful ownership. It upholds anupūrvaśaḥ—sequential unfolding of ancestral entitlement—and assigns proportional responsibility to those who disrupt settled order, without punitive intent but solely for restoration of dharmic balance.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Lineage Completion Process: Reaffirm genealogical documentation and territorial ties
Tenure Integrity Protocol: Validate continuous usage records across three generations
Non-Disturbance Restoration: Realign boundaries and remove encroachment without penalty
Ancestral Memory Reintegration: Acknowledge spiritual-material link between family and land
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority: Ownership rooted in ancestral continuity and uncontested enjoyment is eternally valid; Dharma prevails through recognition of lineage-based rights; Justice serves reintegration alone; Consciousness is the ultimate adjudicator.
